chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you stand at Arafat, draw near to the plateaus, and the plateaus are the mountains, for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The companions of the Arak trees have no Hajj,' meaning those who stand at the Arak trees.

key_terms.الْأَرَاكِ: Arak trees, a type of shrub found in the valley of Mina/Arafat
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the primary station of Hajj
key_terms.لَا حَجَّ لَهُمْ: No Hajj for them (indicating invalidity or deficiency)

ai.seo_question: Where exactly should a pilgrim stand during Wuquf at Arafat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the preferred location for the pivotal standing (wuquf) at Arafat, distinguishing between the elevated plateaus (hisab) and the lower areas with Arak trees. It cites the Prophet’s statement to indicate that standing among the trees renders the Hajj deficient, a view supported by Shia jurists who emphasize the sunnah of occupying the higher ground for better visibility and spiritual focus. This ruling underscores the importance of adhering to the Prophet’s specific guidance in ritual geography to ensure the validity of the Hajj pillar.
